newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris sets split, stock repurchase.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris sets split, stock repurchase.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc said Wednesday directors approved a three-for-one split of the company's common stock, announced a new 3-year $8 billion share repurchase program and declared an unchanged quarterly dividend of $1.20 per share on the pre-split common stock.

To effect the split, two additional common shares will be distributed on April 10 for each share held of record on March 17. Including the split announced today, the company's common stock will have been split seven times since January 1, 1966, with the result that one share in 1966 is now the equivalent of 576 shares, Philip Morris pointed out.
Oppenhiemer analyst Roy Burry said the "timing of the split was a little surprising, but it shouldn't have been" with the recent rise in the price of Philip Morris stock.
The analyst said he had seen a late August split along with a dividend increase
The board also authorized a new 3-year $8 billion share repurchase program, Philip Morris said.
Burry said the new buy-back program is "a nice incrfease ... from the recent (repurchase) rate."
Overall, the announcement was "pleasant news (that came) a little faster than we thought" it would, he said.

The company estimates that the current 3-year $6 billion program, begun in the fourth quarter of 1994, will be completed by the end of the first quarter of 1997. Under that program, the company has bought back 66.3 million shares at an average cost of $84.09 per share through February 25, 1997.
Noting the dividend of $1.20 per pre-split common share is equal to $0.40 a share after giving effect to the split, the compay said it is payable on April 10 to stockholders of record as of March 17.
"Today's actions are consistent with the strategies we announced in 1994 to enhance shareholder value," said chief executive Geoffrey C. Bible.
"Our business growth continues to generate strong earnings and cash flows, enabling us to deliver superior returns to our shareholders." ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
